name: Switch
description: Switch renders a labeled native checkbox with role="switch" and extends checkbox input properties with switch-specific presentation and state options.

elements.name: label
elements.description: The accessible label for the switch. This prop is required.

elements.name: checked / defaultChecked
elements.description: Controls the current state or sets the initial state. Use checked with onChange for a controlled switch, or defaultChecked for an uncontrolled switch.

elements.name: onValue
elements.description: Called with the next boolean state whenever the switch changes.

elements.name: values
elements.description: Displays state text outside the switch. Provide both on and off strings.

elements.name: position
elements.description: Places the switch on the left (default) or right of the label.

elements.name: size
elements.description: Sets the shared component size to sm, md, or lg.

elements.name: tooltip
elements.description: Adds tooltip content as a string, or provides separate on and off messages.

elements.name: colors
elements.description: Sets the thumb color as a tuple of [onColor, offColor]. Custom colors are not applied while disabled.

elements.name: hideLabel
elements.description: Hides the visible label while keeping it available through aria-label.

elements.name: required / disabled
elements.description: Forwards native required and disabled behavior to the checkbox input.

elements.name: containerProps
elements.description: Passes native label properties to the outer switch container.

elements.name: Native checkbox properties
elements.description: Other native checkbox properties such as name, value, id, and aria-describedby are forwarded to the input.

accessibility.general: The component uses a native checkbox with role="switch" inside a label. Native keyboard interaction, focus behavior, form participation, and checked state semantics are preserved.
elements: Always provide a meaningful label. When hideLabel is enabled, the label is exposed through aria-label.
Use values or a tooltip as supplemental state information; the switch role and checked state remain the primary semantic announcement.
Do not rely on custom colors, tooltips, or the visual thumb position alone to communicate whether the switch is on or off.
Use required only when the setting must be enabled for the form to be valid, and provide a clear label explaining the requirement.
